clue.text: Ends as Billy does ? .

definitions.meaning: the stubs or thick ends of things, such as cigarette ends or rifle ends
a billy goat rams with its head, which is what it does

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a man called Billy finishes things.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy is a billy goat here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette's stubs are its leftovers, and a goat's habit is head-ramming; one word covers both senses.

clue.text: They were Bill's prey

parts.note: Bill is Buffalo Bill Cody, who shot great numbers of American bison

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill once hunted these.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffalo Bill earned his nickname hunting bison to feed railway workers.
explanation.definitionFit: American bison, hunted by Buffalo Bill Cody, were his quarry.

clue.text: Are thieves so stupid?

parts.note: plays on the idiom for close friends, as ... as thieves, with the word also meaning dim

explanation.surface: Wondering whether criminals are really that dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'as thick as thieves' means very close; the word also means dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim or dull-witted, and also the word in the idiom for close-knit friends.

clue.text: Possibly cures stab wounds

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Perhaps a remedy for knife injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges CURES STAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Gashes from a cavalry blade are injuries, i.e. wounds.

clue.text: Valuation �by chief artist is held by a friend

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the artist and 'is' are gripped inside the words for 'a friend'

parts.note: a pal is a friend
PRA is President of the Royal Academy, Britain's leading art institution
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend embraces the head of the art world, who gives a valuation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' places the artist and 'is' after the P of 'a friend'. The chief artist is the head of Britain's Royal Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment of worth, as of a painting or property, is a formal estimate of value.

clue.text: An old actor carries one, of course

indicators.note: the word an holds one inside it

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A veteran performer is carrying someone.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merseyside racecourse, home of the Grand National, is a racecourse.

clue.text: A G.P.'s sea-trip? Perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters might form something else

explanation.surface: A doctor wondering about a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges A GPS SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyage or crossing by ship is a journey by sea.

clue.text: Eliot's cruellest of twelve

parts.note: T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land opens by calling one of the year's twelve months the cruellest

explanation.surface: The harshest of a dozen, according to a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month is the one T. S. Eliot called the cruellest of the year's twelve.

clue.text: Old Bob joins the mirth — simply killing

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
laughter is mirth

explanation.surface: An old man named Bob joins in the fun, which is hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simply killing' looks like 'hilarious', but 'killing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchery or massacre is killing on a large scale.

clue.text: End with one thousand bedded in France

indicators.note: put to bed, so placed inside the French bed

parts.note: lit is French for bed
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Concluding with a thousand put to bed in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bedded in France' puts IM in LIT, the French bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary or utmost point is where something ends.

clue.text: Just money-lenders found in Alaska

parts.note: just means fair, as in a fair judgement
banks lend money

explanation.surface: Honest lenders discovered in America's far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only' but is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the interior of the US state of Alaska bears this name.

clue.text: Old Spanish coin with monarch's. head from this region

parts.note: the real was a silver coin of old Spain

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Ancient Spanish money bearing a king's portrait comes from these parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes the first letter of 'monarch's', M.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or domain is a territory or sphere, so it can stand for an area.

clue.text: With odds short this horse would be brilliant

indicators.note: the word for 'brilliant' is cut short of the betting odds

parts.note: to sparkle is to be brilliant
SP is starting price, the odds a racehorse goes off at

explanation.surface: A racing tip: at short odds this horse would shine.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the horse plus SP (starting price) would be SPARKLE. ARKLE was a legendary Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous racehorse, three times winner of the Cheltenham Gold Cup, is named by the clue's horse.

clue.text: Correct about nobleman being on the vehicle

indicators.note: the word for correct goes around the nobleman

parts.note: correct means right
an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: Putting a peer right about the car he's driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the correct word round the nobleman; the definition describes where the lamp sits rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A red lamp at the back of a car or bicycle is fitted to that vehicle.

clue.text: Thrust oneself forward to replace a doubter

indicators.note: to replace the letters is to put them in new places, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A self-assertive person pushing in to take the place of a sceptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replace' signals the anagram of DOUBTER; 'to' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose oneself or push forward unwanted is to intrude assertively.

clue.text: Old RAF man finds members of RN, etc, difficult

indicators.note: the letters are the members of a new grouping, rearranged

parts.note: hard means difficult

explanation.surface: An airman finds sailors and the like hard to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members of' rearranges RNETC to TRENC. Lord Trenchard was the founder of the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Trenchard is known as the father of the Royal Air Force.

clue.text: Composer of band employed in office

definitions.text: Composer of band employed in office

parts.words: Composer of band employed in office
parts.note: not a musician: the material a rubber band is made of, such bands being used in offices

explanation.surface: A musician who writes for a group working in an office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer' and 'band' suggest music, but the composer is what makes up a rubber band.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy rubber material is what an office rubber band is made from.

clue.text: Writer involved in share-outs

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of share-outs are mixed

explanation.surface: An author caught up in dividends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' rearranges SHAREOUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An older word for a female author is a writer.

clue.text: Horse's outfit. Many a vicar is without one

parts.note: C, a hundred in Roman numerals, means many
taken as written

indicators.note: the vicar word is outside, around the one

parts.note: a parson is a vicar
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Ornate equine dress, which plenty of clergymen lack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is without' places I inside PARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental cloth covering for a horse is its finery or trappings.

clue.text: Relative backs favourites-sound in France

indicators.note: the word for favourites is turned back to front

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pet
son is the French word for sound

explanation.surface: A family member supports popular choices for music in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns PETS into STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's child from an earlier marriage is a family member by marriage.

clue.text: The north has bags of simpletons

parts.note: N is north
bags means lots, as does oodles

explanation.surface: Northerners are full of fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The', 'has' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles is old slang for silly people, i.e. fools.

clue.text: Sort of pedal Rommel could have done with

definitions.meaning: a toothed bicycle pedal with a serrated metal frame
Rommel's opponents in North Africa were the British Desert Rats, so a trap for vermin would have helped him

explanation.surface: An odd claim that the German field marshal needed a particular pedal.
explanation.walkthrough: The British 7th Armoured Division, who fought Rommel in the desert, were nicknamed the Desert Rats.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycling pedal named for its toothed look, and a device for catching vermin, here the Desert Rats.

clue.text: Impoverished revolutionary embraces dictator

indicators.note: the revolutionary word holds the dictator in its arms

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary
Duce was Mussolini's title as Italian dictator

explanation.surface: A poor radical hugs a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' wraps the revolutionary round the dictator, Mussolini's Italian title.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced circumstances means poverty, so made poorer.

clue.text: Endorses promise to supply weapon

parts.note: to endorse is to back or support
giving your word is a promise

explanation.surface: Supporting a pledge to provide arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-edged sword is a blade used in fighting.

clue.text: Child painter raised by Russian aristocrat

parts.note: a boy is a child

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A youngster brought up by a Russian nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RA upward to AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the old Russian nobility below the princes was an aristocrat.

clue.text: Playwright to perform in opera, say?

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken like the needed spelling

parts.note: to sing is to perform in opera

explanation.surface: A dramatist going on stage in opera.
explanation.walkthrough: J. M. Synge was an Irish playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: John Millington Synge wrote The Playboy of the Western World, a drama.

clue.text: Arrangement comes in for derision?

indicators.note: the answer comes inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A question whether a ruling will be mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'fOR DERision'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequence or tidy disposition is an orderly arrangement.

clue.text: A golfer's energy

definitions.meaning: a golfer's long shot from the tee

explanation.surface: A player's vigour on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tee shot in golf, and vigour or get-up-and-go.

clue.text: Long tale: without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the tale goes round the point

parts.note: a yarn is a tale
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A lengthy story that is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, putting E inside YARN; 'Long' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine or crave is to long for something.

clue.text: Roman poet given riches and clothes on retirement

parts.note: lucre is money or riches

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the clothes word is read backwards

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothes

explanation.surface: A Roman writer is given wealth and fine garments when he retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on retirement' turns SUIT to TIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin author of De Rerum Natura was a poet of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Came into line again, being set right

definitions.meaning: soldiers dress ranks by lining up, so doing it again
to have a wrong corrected or remedied

explanation.surface: Troops falling back into rank are put right.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers re-dressing ranks line up again; a grievance remedied has been put right.

clue.text: Gertrude put one in the gun

indicators.note: one goes in the gun, the container

parts.note: the Sten was a British submachine gun
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Gertrude loaded a round into the weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Gertrude Stein was an American writer; the STEN was a British wartime gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The American modernist writer had the first name Gertrude.
